feature.name: Recurring invoice templates
feature.description: Auto-send invoices — reusable invoice templates that generate and dispatch invoices automatically on a recurring schedule, for a single-person (teamSize: 1) invoicing product for freelancers, aimed at the US market.

executiveSummary: This report is constrained by a research bundle that returned no usable external data. LedgerLite is a one-person (teamSize: 1) invoicing product for US freelancers, and the feature under evaluation is recurring invoice templates with auto-send. The bundle reports three executed queries — company_identify for FreshBooks, company_identify for Wave, and a company_search — and every one of them failed with an '[object Object]' error payload. As a result the competitors array is empty, enrichResult is null, jobs is empty, and landscape is null. No competitor positioning, pricing, product move, or demand signal for recurring invoicing could be verified from the supplied material. The only defensible conclusions are structural: FreshBooks and Wave are the two named competitor companies to be researched, and the enrichment pipeline must be re-run before any competitive claim in this document is treated as evidence. All statements about positioning, demand, and differentiation below are explicitly flagged as unverified.

gapsAndOpportunities: Unverified: whether FreshBooks or Wave already offer recurring invoice templates with automatic sending, and at what price tier — cannot be determined from this bundle (both company_identify calls errored).
Unverified: whether US freelancers name automatic invoice dispatch as a top pain point. No jobs data (rawBundle.jobs = []) and no landscape data (rawBundle.landscape = null) were returned.
Unverified: whether a single-person team (teamSize: 1) can sustainably maintain scheduled-delivery infrastructure (retries, deliverability, timezone handling) that an auto-send feature implies.

Data-pipeline gap: the '[object Object]' error payload on all three queries prevents diagnosis of whether failures were tool-level, credential-level, or query-level — re-running with full error serialization is a prerequisite to any further analysis.
No market-size, growth-rate, pricing, or adoption data points exist anywhere in the supplied bundle, so no market sizing or revenue opportunity can be stated for this feature.
risks: Evidence risk (high): every external data source in the bundle failed; decisions made on this document alone would rest on zero verified competitor or demand data.

Competitive-parity risk (unverified): recurring invoicing plus auto-send is a mature pattern in accounting and invoicing software generally, and both named competitors may already ship it — this was not verified because enrichment failed.

Scope risk for a solo team (grounded in productData.teamSize = 1): auto-send introduces ongoing operational surface (scheduling, failure retries, email deliverability, refund/void handling) that is harder to support without additional headcount.
Geography-narrowing risk: the bundle covers the US only (productData.geography = 'US'), so any conclusion drawn here should not be extended to other markets without separate data.

Stakeholder risk: because planSummary is null and the bundle is empty, presenting this as a complete market analysis could create false confidence; it should be circulated as a failed-research report, not a market finding.
Competitor-set risk (unverified): limiting the field to FreshBooks and Wave was an input assumption, not a validated finding, and may omit the most direct competitors for US freelancer invoicing.
